leading_positions.synthesis: Ten of eleven round-1 files name B006 as the preferred single prize part, each with the same laureate set (Autor, Hanson, Katz) and citations built around labour demand, wage inequality or wage structure, and local labour-market adjustment to technology and trade. Shared reasoning: a conceptual framework (skill demand, tasks) paired with design-based evidence on import competition; a record of roughly 10 to 30 years of replication and critique; reach into labour, trade, macro and policy. Not shared: how settled the Katz-versus-Dorn choice is. Several supporters (Boppart, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Fredriksson, Strömberg, Teorell) say they would consider or accept an Autor-Dorn-Hanson variant if the committee wants a trade-shock-centred citation, while Andersson, Dreber, Enflo and Krusell keep Katz and describe the Dorn exclusion as a cost of the three-name cap. Nearly all supporters list the same reservations (attribution, Goldin/Acemoglu adjacency, persistence of China-shock effects). Several supporters changed from different opening first choices after reading colleagues' openings (Andersson, Dreber, Krusell, Hassler), which the files state explicitly. The set differs from the Autor-Hanson two-name proposal Friberg described and from the Dorn variant; neither of those is an explicit preferred configuration in round 1, so neither is counted as support.

Friberg is the only member whose round-1 preferred configuration is B007 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley). His case: political economics made institutions endogenous and testable, attribution is comparatively clean, the programme is about three decades old, and it spans public economics, development and macro. He names empirical identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects as the main weakness, concedes that Besley is a closer call than Persson and Tabellini, and says the case should survive without Krusell's and his own support. B007 is a listed alternative for Enflo, Hassler, Krusell and Teorell, but none prefers it in round 1. The files that mention it cite its cleaner credit as a strength and weaker identification or proximity to the 2024 institutions prize as reservations. Friberg lists B006 as an alternative and treats it as scientifically strong, with the open issue being credit division and whether it is one discovery or two.

areas_of_agreement: Every file that discusses B006 judges the work influential, conceptually and empirically substantive, and mature enough to have been tested; the contested points concern the size and persistence of the China-shock effects rather than whether the effects exist.

Members across fields state that attribution under the three-name cap is B006's main weakness, and that Levy and Murnane (and Acemoglu's task-model theory) lie outside the credited names, so any citation should not claim origination of the whole task framework.
There is broad agreement that the citation should be worded around what has been shown (labour demand, wage structure, local adjustment) and should not assert a settled long-run magnitude.
B007's attribution is described as cleaner than B006's, and B004's as more diffuse than B006's (eight credited names, no clean trio), by members across both camps.
Members say they are weighing opening support counts as neither merit nor a substitute for scientific assessment (stated explicitly by Krusell, Strömberg, Hjalmarsson and others).
scientific_disputes: Whether B006 is one discovery (how technology and trade shift labour demand and adjustment costs) or two adjacent lines (technology/skill premium and trade shock); Strömberg, Dreber, Enflo, Fredriksson, Friberg, Teorell and Hassler all flag this, and Andersson argues one citation can hold both.
How far shift-share inference concerns and the persistence/external validity debate on China-shock effects qualify the B006 evidence; supporters treat it as a question of magnitude, not existence.

B007: how well cross-country evidence on constitutional and electoral-rule effects meets modern identification standards (Friberg, Boppart, Strömberg, Teorell, Enflo), versus the view that the theory, state-capacity work and later quasi-experimental extensions stand on firmer ground.

B032: whether the collateral-constraint mechanism is sufficiently confirmed given limited direct tests of the original model and support that is largely indirect, and how distinct it is from the work recognised by the 2022 prize.
B004: the framework's empirical standing after 2008 and the 2021-23 inflation, and whether the estimated DSGE strand is part of the discovery.
B034: whether a methods toolkit (BLP-style estimation and dynamic industry models) carries as much scientific consequence as a framework-plus-evidence prize.
attribution_disputes: B006 third name: Katz (skill-premium and education-technology framework) versus Dorn (co-author of the China-shock papers), or a two-name Autor-Hanson set as in Friberg's description; the supporters' files disagree on how decisive this is.

Katz's marginal credit given his education-technology work with Goldin (2023 prize); members differ on whether this reduces his claim or only calls for precise wording, with Strömberg and Teorell calling his claim the most exposed or the closest call.
Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu on the task framework: whether a Katz-Autor-Hanson citation can fairly describe the task contribution, or should avoid it.
B007: whether Besley's work is distinct from and as well supported as the Persson-Tabellini core, given some joint work with Persson.

B004: any trio from the eight credited names (Taylor, Woodford, Calvo, with Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets omitted) is described as contestable, and members differ on whether a narrower pricing-and-policy-rule citation could resolve it (Andersson).
B034: how to credit the dynamic-game strand and Bresnahan relative to Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (Fredriksson).
maturity_disputes: B006 maturity is generally not contested: skill-premium work about three decades old, task framework over two decades, China-shock papers over a decade. The live issue is whether the persistence debate on China-shock effects should weigh on timing or on merit.

Whether adjacency to the 2023 (Goldin) and 2024 (Acemoglu) prizes affects the marginal case for B006: some members treat it as a framing and timing matter only (Fredriksson, Hjalmarsson, Hassler, Krusell), others ask that the committee state what B006 adds (Teorell, Dreber, Andersson).
B007: whether the 2024 institutions prize makes timing less comfortable, versus the view that the formal political-economics programme is distinct (Friberg, Hassler, Krusell).
B012 is described as having cleaner attribution but a shorter record (Strömberg); B032 as a mature mechanism but a single-paper foundation with indirect empirical support (Hassler, Fredriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Krusell: Persson, credited on B007, is at IIES, his home institute; Krusell flags B007 and prefers B006 in round 1. He also reports field proximity to B006's skill-premium strand (capital-skill complementarity), with no tie to a credited name.
Boppart: long-running collaborations with Krusell (secretary) and Hassler (chair), both IIES colleagues; field proximity to growth and reallocation; no tie to B006 laureates.

Hassler (chair): co-authored with Boppart and Friberg; IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart; frequent co-author of Krusell; own social-mobility research is topically near B050, which he ranks seventh and does not prefer; no tie to B006 credited names apparent from the supplied profile.
Friberg: discloses marriage to Magdalena Andersson (a public fact) and a co-authored price-setting paper with Hassler and Ellingsen; no candidate-specific tie to B007 is apparent.
Teorell: field proximity of his research on institutions and state capacity to B007 (an alternative); Stockholm University colleague of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart.
Dreber: Harvard Kennedy School fellowship 2009-2017 while Katz is at Harvard; no co-authorship or collaboration with any credited B006 name.
Fredriksson: empirical labour economist whose class-size work is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background; methodological proximity to B006 disclosed.
Enflo: research on electrification and labour markets is topically adjacent to B006; no personal tie to credited names.
Hjalmarsson: labour-economics field proximity to B006; presented the 2023 Goldin announcement (a role, not a tie to a candidate).
Strömberg: adjunct appointment at Chicago Booth, disclosed for transparency; B001 adjacent to his corporate-finance field.
Andersson: collegial SSE affiliations and COVID-policy co-authorship, none involving a shortlisted candidate.
All of the above are disclosed and not adjudicated in this summary.
questions_for_round2: For each B006 supporter: if the committee must fix one third laureate, is it Katz or Dorn, and what specific evidence of distinct, non-overlapping contribution (including relative to the Goldin-Katz work) would change your answer? Would anyone support a two-name Autor-Hanson prize?

Can supporters and Friberg and Strömberg jointly draft one citation that (a) states whether this is one discovery or two, (b) avoids claiming origination of the task framework, and (c) avoids restating the 2023 and 2024 citations? If not, where exactly does the drafting fail?

Does the B006 evidence need to resolve the shift-share and persistence debate before the prize is justified, or is the established finding (effects on labour demand and local adjustment) sufficient? Which specific results should the committee treat as settled?

Friberg: is your preference for B007 mainly about cleaner credit and breadth, or is there a scientific reason B006 should rank below it? Other members who list B007 as an alternative (Enflo, Hassler, Krusell, Teorell): what would need to be shown about identification and the 2024 prize for you to prefer B007, and does the case stand independently of any disclosed ties?
Does any member wish to propose a two-part configuration (for example adding B034, B012 or B004 alongside B006), and if so on what criteria and with what laureate division?

For members whose preferred option moved after reading openings (Andersson, Dreber, Krusell, Hassler), which specific argument changed your assessment, and would that argument survive if the other members' positions were not known to you?
summary.chair_observation: This summary is a process record, not a ruling. On the round-1 files, ten of eleven members explicitly prefer the same three-name B006 set, and one prefers B007; the chair is among the ten. The files also state that several members changed preferences after reading others' openings, and some peer responses refer to earlier opening rankings that the round-1 preferred configurations now supersede. Because the count measures convergence rather than merit, round 2 should test whether the agreement rests on the stated criteria, not on movement toward the leading option. The remaining open issues are narrower than the headline count suggests: the Katz-versus-Dorn division of credit, how one citation should handle the technology and trade strands and the Goldin and Acemoglu adjacency, and whether the B007 minority position rests on a scientific disagreement or on credit and timing preferences.
